'''Joseph Hillel Silverman''' (born March 27, 1955)<ref name=Bios2007>
{{Citation |date=September 2007 |title=Biographies of Candidates 2007 |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |volume=54 |issue=8 |pages=1043–1057 |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200708/tx070801043p.pdf |access-date=2009-05-25 }}</ref> is a professor of mathematics at [[Brown University]]<ref>[https://www.brown.edu/academics/math/faculty Brown University Mathematics Faculty], retrieved 2020-01-13.</ref> working in [[arithmetic geometry]], [[arithmetic dynamics]], and [[cryptography]].

==Biography==
Joseph Silverman received an [[Bachelor of Science|Sc.B.]] from Brown University in 1977 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from [[Harvard University]] in 1982 under the direction of [[John Tate (mathematician)|John Tate]]. He taught at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|M.I.T.]] (1982–1986) and at [[Boston University]] (1986–1988) before taking a position at Brown in 1988.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Curriculum Vite |url=https://vivo.brown.edu/docs/j/johsilve_cv.pdf?dt=231315106 |access-date=August 31, 2024 |website=vivo.brown.edu}}</ref>

Silverman has published more than 150 research articles, written or coauthored eight books, and edited three conference proceedings; his work has been cited more than 7500 times, by over 4000 distinct authors.<ref>[https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/2006/mathscinet/search/author.html?mrauthid=162205 MathSciNet author citations]</ref>  He has served on the editorial boards of ''[[Algebra and Number Theory]]'' and ''[[New York Journal of Mathematics]]''.<ref>[https://msp.org/ant/about/journal/editorial.html Editorial board of Algebra and Number Theory], retrieved 2020-01-13.</ref><ref>[http://nyjm.albany.edu/edboard.htm Editorial Board of New York Journal of Mathematics], retrieved 2020-01-13.</ref>

==Industry==
In 1996, Silverman, along with [[Jeffrey Hoffstein]], [[Jill Pipher]] and [[Daniel Lieman]], founded NTRU Cryptosystems, Inc. to market their cryptographic algorithms, [[NTRUEncrypt]] and [[NTRUSign]].

==Awards==
In 2012 Silverman became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-07-20.</ref> He was a [[List of Guggenheim Fellowships awarded in 1998|Guggenheim Fellow (1998)]] and is a recipient of the NES MAA Award for Distinguished Teaching (2011).<ref>{{cite web | title=Awards | url=https://www.northeastern.maa.org/awards }}</ref>
In 2022, he was an [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] and spoke on the topic [[Arithmetic_dynamics|"Arithmetic Dynamics."]]

==American Mathematical Society==
Silverman has been a member of governance of the [[American Mathematical Society]], including stints on the AMS Council (2008-2011),<ref>[http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/council-past.html]</ref> the AMS Executive Committee (2009-2013),<ref>[http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/ec-past.html]</ref>  and the AMS Board of Trustees (2015-2025).<ref>[http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/bt-past.html]</ref>

==Books==
Silverman has written two graduate texts on [[elliptic curve]]s, ''The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves'' (1986) and ''Advanced Topics in the Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves'' (1994). For these two books he received a [[Steele Prize]] for Mathematical Exposition from the [[American Mathematical Society]], which cited them by saying that “Silverman's volumes have become standard references on one of the most exciting areas of algebraic geometry and number theory.” Silverman has also written four undergraduate texts: ''Rational Points on Elliptic Curves'' (1992, co-authored with [[John Tate (mathematician)|John Tate]]), ''A Friendly Introduction to Number Theory'' (3rd ed. 2005), ''An Introduction to Mathematical Cryptography'' (2008, co-authored with Jeffrey Hoffstein and Jill Pipher), and ''Abstract Algebra: An Integrated Approach'' (2022). Additional graduate-level texts authored by Silverman are ''Diophantine Geometry: An Introduction'' (2000, co-authored with [[Marc Hindry]]) and ''The Arithmetic of Dynamical Systems'' (2007).
